Test Description: This testcase validates multi-channel transmit and receive operation on the DWC Ethernet QoS IP (Ethernet0) across all four DMA channels (CH0 through CH3). The test exercises the full MAC, MTL, and DMA subsystem configuration including MAC speed and duplex mode selection, MAC address programming, MTL TX/RX queue operation modes with quantum weight assignment, RX queue-to-DMA channel mapping, and per-channel DMA descriptor ring setup. TX and RX descriptors are preloaded for all four channels. The test sequentially activates each DMA channel starting from CH3 down to CH0, triggering the Ethernet VIP sequencer for each channel. Each channel is expected to transfer 10 packets, and cumulative TX/RX packet counts are validated at thresholds of 10, 20, 30, and 40 packets respectively. Conditional logic supports RX descriptor ring reload when the tail pointer reaches the end of the ring. The test completes after all four channels have been validated.
Test Steps / Procedure:
Step 1: Initialize the interrupt controller and enable all interrupts.
Step 2: Select the Ethernet interface based on the build configuration.
Step 3: Configure the MAC Configuration register for the desired speed and duplex mode.
Step 4: Configure MAC Extended Configuration, Packet Filter, RX Queue Control registers, and VLAN Tag Control.
Step 5: Program MAC Address registers for multi-channel address filtering.
Step 6: Mask MMC IPC RX interrupts.
Step 7: Configure MTL Operation Mode and TX Queue Operation Mode for all four queues. Assign quantum weights.
Step 8: Configure RX Queue Operation Mode and RX Queue Control registers.
Step 9: Configure MTL Queue Interrupt Control Status for all four queues.
Step 10: Configure DMA Mode and DMA Channel Control for CH0.
Step 11: Set DMA TX Control and RX Control for all four channels.
Step 12: Program TX and RX Descriptor List Addresses for all four channels.
Step 13: Set TX Descriptor Ring Length and RX Control2 for all four channels.
Step 14: Set TX Descriptor Tail Pointers for all four channels.
Step 15: Enable DMA interrupts for all four channels.
Step 16: Configure RX Queue-to-DMA Channel mapping and verify by reading back.
Step 17: Set RX Queue Control registers for all four queues.
Step 18: Preload TX descriptors for all four channels.
Step 19: Preload RX descriptors for all four channels.
Step 20: Configure power management register.
Step 21: Enable CH3 RX and trigger VIP sequencer.
Step 22: Poll and validate cumulative packet count reaches 10.
Step 23: Enable CH2 and trigger VIP sequencer.
Step 24: Poll and validate cumulative packet count reaches 20.
Step 25: Enable CH1 and trigger VIP sequencer.
Step 26: Poll and validate cumulative packet count reaches 30.
Step 27: Enable CH0 and trigger VIP sequencer.
Step 28: Poll and validate cumulative packet count reaches 40.
Step 29: Update CH2 and CH3 TX Descriptor Tail Pointers.
Step 30: Wait for completion delay and finish the test.

Validation / Acceptance Criteria:
1. After CH3 activation, cumulative RX=10 and TX=10.
2. After CH2 activation, cumulative RX=20 and TX=20.
3. After CH1 activation, cumulative RX=30 and TX=30.
4. After CH0 activation, cumulative RX=40 and TX=40.
5. RX descriptor conditional reload when tail pointer reaches end of ring.
6. MTL RXQ DMA Map0 readback verification.
7. Test must complete without hanging in any polling loop.
Remarks: The test supports multiple speed configurations (10M, 100M, 1G) and duplex modes (Full, Half) selectable via build-time configuration. Default is 1G Full Duplex. Channels are activated sequentially from CH3 to CH0. Each channel handles 10 packets for a total of 40.
